tools.description: Generate speech from text with HeyGen Voice. Use a voice_id from list_voices: type=public for HeyGen's voices, type=private for the workspace's clones. Set language to the text's ISO 639-1 code or omit it to detect. Set with_timestamps for word and character timings. A 429 for the workspace's daily Turbo Free limit (retryable false) stands until the limit resets: explain it, never retry. A 429 saying free capacity is full (retryable true) is temporary: back off and retry once. After any other generation error or timeout, ask the user before another generation; never retry automatically. Widget-capable chat hosts also display an inline audio player when its bundle is available. Clients without widgets receive the audio URL. Listening, seeking, and downloading do not require another generation call. The player Regenerate button makes one user-requested call that replays the original text, voice, language and speed (the model is chosen for the plan again); do not repeat that call from the conversation. tools.description:
Create a Cinematic Avatar video: a 4–15 second clip of one to three avatar looks driven by a natural-language prompt, plus optional reference images, videos or audio. Use it only when the user explicitly asks for Cinematic Avatar; a style word like "cinematic" is not such a request. There is no script or voice input, so exact wording is not guaranteed: describe the scene, the action and any words the person says in the prompt. A presenter speaking to camera uses create_video_from_avatar; other visual productions of 30 seconds or less use text_to_video. If it fails with plan_upgrade_required, explain that Cinematic Avatar is not included in the account's current plan, offer a talking-avatar video with create_video_from_avatar instead, and wait for the user's answer. Do not retry, switch tools on your own, or promote purchases or upgrades. If a public avatar is rejected, tell the user that Cinematic Avatar cannot use public studio avatars and let them choose one of their own avatars or an AI-generated public avatar; do not substitute one. Media inputs take a HeyGen asset_id or a public https URL, never a local or sandbox path (/mnt/data/..., file://); import or upload the file first and pass its asset_id.
Poll get_video with the returned videoId until completed or failed; return video_url on completion.
Use a server-provided retry delay, otherwise wait 30 seconds between polls. After five minutes,
return the latest status and available video link so the user can resume later. Never resubmit
creation to check progress. For open-ended creative production, use create_video_agent instead.

tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.title: Submit feedback to HeyGen
tools.description:
Submit concise product feedback to HeyGen after the user gives
feedback or you observe a meaningful terminal failure that did not recover. Set source=user
only for feedback the user actually expressed; use source=agent for your own observation.
Always include `toolName` and `resourceIds` when a project, session, video, or other
resource exists for this issue — a report with no resource ID and no tool name is usually
not root-causable later. Include the exact observed error, but never credentials, raw media,
unrelated conversation text, or an invented cause or user opinion. For usability or
performance complaints (e.g. "too slow", "stuck", "hung"), also include `pipelineStep`
(which stage was slow — compose, magic_edit, render_video, or other) and `elapsedSeconds`
(how long it actually took), and set `expectedBaseline` when the user states or implies
what they expected (e.g. "usually under 2 minutes", "faster in the web app") — these turn a
vague "too slow" into a diagnosable report. Do not report expected validation, consent, or
billing guidance unless the user says it is a problem. If you know the current host
application and surface, provide `reportedClientName` and `reportedClientSurface`;
otherwise omit them. Report the host, such as ChatGPT, Codex desktop, Codex CLI, Claude, or
Grok, never the model name and never an inferred client. Submit once per issue and do not
retry a failed feedback submission in a loop. Submission is best effort and does not confirm
durable storage or operator review. Do not automatically report historical failures found while browsing.
Follow the client consent policy and briefly tell the user after submitting feedback.

tools.description:
Record that you activated a HeyGen plugin skill, for product
analytics. Call this once per skill per conversation: the first time you use a skill, before its
first other HeyGen tool call. Later work with the same skill, such as edits, revisions,
regenerations, and re-reading the skill, is the same activation, so do not call this again for a
skill already recorded in this conversation. Pass the skill's technical name exactly as written in
the `name` field of its SKILL.md (for example `ugc-product`), never its display name, with a
structured description of the request: the closest `requestType`, the kinds of input the user
supplied in `inputTypes`, and the requested length, aspect ratio, language, and platforms when
known. Set `routedFrom` to heygen_workflows when that skill sent you here. Use only these
structured fields: never include the user's words, names, brands, URLs, file names, or other
conversation content. Recording is best effort; if it fails or this tool is unavailable, continue
the task and do not retry or tell the user.

user has the skill's final output, or the skill cannot deliver it. Every track_skill_activation call
gets exactly one matching completion; later revisions of a completed skill do not record another.
Pass the same `skillName` (the `name` field of its SKILL.md, never its display name) and the
`activationId` that track_skill_activation returned, when there is one. Set `outcome` to success only
when the user received the skill's final output as the skill describes it. Anything that keeps the
user from that output is a failure, even if you delivered partial results: for example, if the skill
composes three clips into one video, the clips generated, but no sandbox was available to stitch them
and you returned the raw clips, record failure with `failureReason` sandbox_unavailable. If the user
changes course or stops before the final output, record failure with user_cancelled. On failure,
choose the closest `failureReason` and, when useful, add a short technical `failureDetail` such as
"could not open sandbox to stitch 3 clips"; omit both on success. Use only these structured fields:
never include the user's words, names, brands, URLs, file names, or other conversation content.
Recording is best effort; if it fails or this tool is unavailable, continue the task and do not retry
or tell the user.

skillName.description: The completed skill's exact name, as passed to track_skill_activation.
skillName.title: Skillname

outcome.description: success only when the user received the skill's final output; failure when anything kept them from it.
outcome.title: Outcome

activationId.description: The activationId track_skill_activation returned for this skill, when it returned one.
activationId.title: Activationid

failureReason.description: Required when outcome is failure; omit on success. sandbox_unavailable: no code or execution environment to stitch, edit, or render. generation_failed: a HeyGen generation failed or returned unusable output. tool_error: a tool call errored or was unavailable. insufficient_credits: out of credits, quota, or plan limit. content_moderation: blocked by moderation or policy. missing_input: the user did not provide required input or assets. user_cancelled: the user stopped or changed course before the final output. timeout: generation or processing did not finish in time. unsupported_request: the skill cannot do what was asked. other: none fits.
failureReason.title: Failurereason

failureDetail.description: Optional, only with failure: a short technical phrase such as "could not open sandbox to stitch 3 clips". Never the user's words, names, brands, URLs, or file names.
failureDetail.title: Failuredetail

tools.name: track_user_intent
tools.title: Record HeyGen user intent
tools.description:
Record what the user wants from HeyGen, why they want it, and which
HeyGen tools will carry it out, for product analytics. Call this once for each new goal the user
brings in a conversation, after you have picked the tools and before the first of them runs. A
new goal is a different thing to make or do, such as a second video on a new topic or a switch
from a video to a voice clone. Steps needed to deliver it, such as picking or first creating an
avatar, are part of the goal. Revisions, edits, retries, and follow-up questions about the same
result are the same goal, so do not call this again for them, even when they use other tools.

Write `intent` as clearly and specifically as you can, in one to three English sentences of your
own words: what the user wants to make or do and any requirements they gave, such as length,
format, style, language, platform, and the kinds of input they supplied. For example: "A
30-second vertical TikTok video with a friendly female presenter showing a skincare serum, made
from the user's product photo, in English." Do not categorize or shorten it into labels.

Write `useCase` as one English sentence on the job the user is trying to get done with it: the
business or personal purpose and who it is for, such as "Promote the user's own skincare business
to young adults on social media" or "Publish an audiobook of the user's novel". Set
`useCaseBasis` to `stated` when the user said it, or `inferred` when you worked it out from what
they shared, such as their product, audience, channel, or role. If there is nothing to go on,
leave both out rather than guess.

In both, describe kinds of things rather than naming them: leave out people's names, brands,
company and product names, URLs, emails, phone numbers, file names, and script or quoted text.

List in `toolNames`, by exact tool name and in order, the HeyGen tools that carry out the goal:
the ones that create, change, or delete something for the user, such as `create_speech` for text
to speech, `convert_speech` for speech to speech, `create_ai_clipping` for clips from a long
video, or `create_digital_twin` then `create_video_from_avatar`. When the goal only looks
something up, such as listing videos or checking credits, list the tool that answers it. Leave
out supporting calls, such as listing voices, looks, or avatars to choose from, uploading assets,
consent steps, and status polling.

Recording is best effort; if it fails or this tool is unavailable, continue the task and do not
retry or tell the user.

intent.description: What the user wants, as clearly as possible, in one to three English sentences of your own words.
intent.title: Intent

toolNames.description: The HeyGen tools that carry out this goal, by exact tool name, in order; skip supporting calls and polling.
toolNames.title: Toolnames

useCase.description: The job the user is trying to get done with it, stated or inferred from the conversation; omit if unknown.
useCase.title: Usecase

useCaseBasis.description: stated when the user said the use case; inferred when you worked it out.
useCaseBasis.title: Usecasebasis

tools.name: continue_subscription_cancellation
tools.title: Discuss Subscription Options
tools.description: Pass the user's latest cancellation feedback or question from the chat to HeyGen's existing retention conversation. Use the flowId returned by cancel_subscription and the user's own message; never invent feedback or call without a new user turn. If the returned snapshot.state is 'confirm', immediately call show_subscription_action with action='cancel' without another chat confirmation question. Otherwise send the returned cancellation reply directly to the user, preserving its wording. Do not add an attribution such as 'HeyGen says', a preamble, or quotation marks. Only offer terms returned by HeyGen are valid. This tool does not display a widget. When an offer is ready, call show_subscription_action with action='offer'. If the user reaffirms cancellation, including 'yes' to a cancellation question, or explicitly wants to skip further questions or offers, call show_subscription_action with action='cancel' instead of continuing the conversation. An affirmative answer to an offer or unrelated question is not cancellation intent. Neither this conversation nor the display tool changes billing; only explicit widget clicks accept offers or confirm cancellation. Do not automatically retry a timed-out message; reopen the existing flow to check status.

tools.name: lookup_videos
tools.title: Look Up Videos
tools.description: List video IDs and metadata as paginated JSON without opening a widget. Use this for selecting a video for a follow-up tool, including 'show my latest video'. Choose the newest completed item and verify it with get_video before presenting it. Explain if a newer failed attempt was skipped; if none are playable, report that without opening failed players. For browsing the library, use list_videos instead.

limit.description: Maximum videos per page
limit.title: Limit

token.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response
token.title: Token

title.description: Filter videos by title substring
title.title: Title

tools.name: show_subscription_action
tools.title: Show Subscription Action Card
tools.description: Display a subscription action card for an existing cancellation flow. Do not call for the initial general cancellation request: start with cancel_subscription and relay Cicero's opening question in chat. Use action='offer' only after Cicero returns an eligible offer; use action='cancel' immediately when Cicero indicates cancellation confirmation, the user reaffirms cancellation (including 'yes' to a cancellation question), or explicitly declines further questions/offers and wants to proceed. Do not ask another confirmation question in chat before opening this card. Reads current status and terms; it cannot apply an offer or cancel billing. The user must click an explicit action in the card.

action.description: 'cancel' shows the cancellation confirmation card; 'offer' shows the option returned in the conversation.
action.title: Action

tools.name: create_speech_without_player
tools.title: Create Speech Without Player
tools.description: Generate speech from text with HeyGen Voice. Use a voice_id from list_voices: type=public for HeyGen's voices, type=private for the workspace's clones. Voice IDs from older HeyGen voice catalogs are refused. Returns an audio URL (WAV by default) and its duration in seconds. Omit model unless the user explicitly asks for one: the server uses heygen-voice-1-turbo-free on a free MCP plan, which speaks instant voices only (every public voice is instant), and heygen-voice-1 otherwise. Set language to the text's ISO 639-1 code or omit it to detect. Set with_timestamps for word and character timings. A 429 for the workspace's daily Turbo Free limit (retryable false) stands until the limit resets: explain it, never retry. A 429 saying free capacity is full (retryable true) is temporary: back off and retry once. After any other generation error or timeout, ask the user before another generation; never retry automatically. Never opens the audio player on any host: returns the same audio URL JSON as create_speech, so use it when the user does not need to listen inline, such as when a skill or workflow generates several clips in parallel. Use create_speech when the user should listen in the inline player. Each call consumes speech quota; one agreed script authorizes one call.

voiceId.description: Voice ID from list_voices. IDs from older HeyGen voice catalogs are refused.
voiceId.title: Voiceid

text.description: Text to synthesize. Instant voices accept caller-supplied IPA, such as <pron ipa="/ˈækmi/">Acme</pron>. Respelling cues are not supported. Unsupported IPA returns HTTP 400. Pronunciation requires an available pronunciation-capable model. Instant voices perform audio tags in square brackets, such as [laughs], [whispers], or [sad]; see https://developers.heygen.com/docs/voices/heygen-voice-speech#audio-tags for the supported tags. Bracketed text that is not a supported tag is usually not spoken; to have those words spoken, remove the square brackets. Professional voices do not perform audio tags. Professional voices accept <break time="Xs"/> pauses (seconds, up to 5 per pause, e.g. <break time="0.5s"/>); other SSML, and break tags for an instant voice clone, are not supported.
text.title: Text

outputFormat.description: Optional audio output: encoding pcm (signed little-endian PCM16), mp3, ulaw, or alaw; mono only. sample_rate_hertz: 8000, 16000, 22050, 24000, 44100, or 48000 for pcm/mp3 (default 44100); ulaw/alaw require 8000 (default). MP3 bitrate_bps: 32000/48000/64000 below 32000 Hz (default 64000), or 64000/96000/128000/192000 at 44100/48000 Hz (default 128000). Omit for the existing WAV file or SSE stream of base64 WAV parts. When supplied, /tts/stream returns raw audio bytes and does not support with_timestamps.

model.description: Omit to let the server choose: heygen-voice-1-turbo-free on a free MCP plan, heygen-voice-1 otherwise. Set only when the user explicitly asks for a model. heygen-voice-1 speaks instant and professional voices; heygen-voice-1-turbo (lower latency) and heygen-voice-1-turbo-free (no charge, daily limits, shared capacity) speak instant voices only.
model.title: Model

applyTextNormalization.description: Text normalization rewrites numbers, currencies, dates, and other written forms as spoken words before synthesis. Applies to instant voices, including Turbo, and professional voices. on normalizes text in Arabic, Chinese, English, French, German, Hebrew, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, and Vietnamese; text in any other language is spoken as written. off speaks all text as written. auto (default) lets HeyGen Voice decide and currently behaves as on. Pronunciation dictionaries, inline IPA, audio tags, and break tags are not affected.
applyTextNormalization.title: Applytextnormalization

pronunciationDictionary.description: Optional term-to-IPA dictionary, such as {"Acme": "/ˈækmi/"}. Use enclosing slashes for each IPA value. Matches whole terms without case sensitivity. Inline pronunciation takes precedence. Supports instant voices on heygen-voice-1 and heygen-voice-1-turbo when pronunciation is available. Omit expressiveness_boost to use 0.5, or supply a value from 0.0 to 1.0.
pronunciationDictionary.title: Pronunciationdictionary

language.description: Language of `text` as a lowercase ISO 639-1 code, such as `en` or `zh`. HeyGen Voice has no regional accents, so a regional tag such as `en-US` or `zh-HK` fails with `invalid_parameter`. Omit it to detect the language from `text`. A confident reading that matches the letters of `text` is used, and the request fails with `invalid_parameter` if HeyGen Voice does not speak that language. Otherwise the first of these that HeyGen Voice speaks is used: the language the voice was created in, if `text` is written in that language's script; a less certain reading that a second reading of `text` without its numbers and brand names agrees with; the usual language of the script `text` is mostly written in, such as English for Latin letters; and, only when that script has no usual language, the reading itself. If none of them applies, the request fails with `invalid_parameter`. The `Content-Language` response header names the language used.
language.title: Language

expressivenessBoost.description: Expressiveness boost for instant voices, from 0.0 to 1.0. Omit for professional voices. Omitted values use 0.5 with pronunciation and 1.0 otherwise. The boost is not applied when text contains an audio tag other than [pause].
expressivenessBoost.title: Expressivenessboost

seed.description: Optional best-effort deterministic generation seed for professional clones. Ignored for instant clones.
seed.title: Seed

speed.description: Speech speed multiplier for professional clones. Ignored for instant clones, including Turbo.
speed.title: Speed

pitchShift.description: Pitch shift in semitones for professional clones. Ignored for instant clones.
pitchShift.title: Pitchshift

pitchVariance.description: Pitch variation multiplier for professional clones; 1.0 preserves the voice default. Ignored for instant clones.
pitchVariance.title: Pitchvariance

withTimestamps.description: Include character and word timings in the response.
withTimestamps.title: Withtimestamps

tools.name: cancel_subscription
tools.title: Start Subscription Cancellation Conversation
tools.description: Start HeyGen's cancellation conversation in the chat. This tool does not open a widget or change billing. For a general request such as 'I want to cancel my HeyGen subscription', call this tool with skipRetention=false and send the returned opening question directly to the user, preserving its wording. Do not add an attribution such as 'HeyGen says', a preamble, or quotation marks. A reason is optional: forward only feedback already supplied. Set skipRetention=true only if the user explicitly asks to skip questions/offers or go directly to confirmation. Use an existing flowId to resume without replaying the opening turn. Continue new user turns with continue_subscription_cancellation. Display show_subscription_action only for an eligible offer or cancellation confirmation.

tools.title: Check Avatar Creation Status
tools.description: Report in plain text how the user's avatar creation is progressing — photo training, footage training, consent validation, voice cloning, and the preview video. Call when the user asks whether their avatar is ready. Requires the job ids from the guided flow; it starts nothing and changes nothing.
